insights.claim: trainer-operator uses label-selector-scoped informer caches and disabled Namespace caching to prevent memory exhaustion from unrelated cluster resources.
insights.reasoning: The manager configures ByObject label selectors on Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and ValidatingWebhookConfigurations scoped to the trainer-managed label. Namespace is explicitly excluded from the cache via DisableFor, and StripUnusedFields reduces per-object memory. This is a defense against the OOMKill anti-pattern documented in the inline code comment.

insights.claim: The operator uses a platform-aware dependency check that distinguishes OpenShift (requires JobSetOperator CR health) from vanilla Kubernetes (requires only JobSet CRD).
insights.reasoning: cluster.DetectClusterType from odh-platform-utilities determines the platform, then the operator runs different prerequisite checks. On OpenShift, it validates JobSetOperator installation, CR presence, and health before checking JobSet CRD. On vanilla Kubernetes, only the JobSet CRD check is performed. This pattern enables the same operator binary to work across different Kubernetes distributions.

insights.claim: Metrics endpoint on port 8080 is served over plaintext HTTP with no authentication, relying entirely on network-level access control.
insights.reasoning: SecureServing is explicitly set to false in the controller-runtime manager options. The metrics endpoint exposes operational data without any authentication or encryption. While health/readiness probes are intentionally unauthenticated, the metrics endpoint may expose sensitive operational information. This is a deliberate design choice noted in the analyzer evidence.
